Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Transport GSA launches digital platform to fight Non-Tariff Barriers Source : Joy Business 23 November 2026 10:15am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) has developed a digital Non-Tariff Barriers (NTB) Reporting and Resolution Platform in collaboration with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, with support from Trade Mark Africa to enhance cargo movements from the ports.
Speaking at a media engagement, the CEO Prof. Ransford Gyampo said the movement of goods is often impeded by non-tariff barriers which cost traders’ time and money — but most are never reported and never resolved.
“With the NTB platform, anyone can report a barrier, from the Web, WhatsApp, social media and a simple USSD Code,” he said.
The platform will facilitate the reporting, monitoring and resolution of trade-related barriers.
The NTB platform is part of a wider digital transformation drive. The Authority advanced the integration of shipper registration onto the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) to strengthen its shipper database and enhance evidence-based regulatory oversight.
Previously, the absence of a comprehensive and reliable database of shippers constrained the Authority’s ability to discharge its regulatory responsibilities and respond to shippers’ needs.
Prof. Gyampo said the Authority has expanded its operations to 24 hours in support of Government’s 24-Hour Economy agenda, after preparing and presenting a policy paper to the Presidency outlining its contribution.
“The Government of Ghana’s 24-Hour Economy Policy represents a transformative national agenda aimed at repositioning the country as a competitive, export-driven and industrialized economy capable of sustaining continuous economic activity,” he said.
Other digital and trade facilitation gains in 2026 included sustained transit corridor monitoring, which contributed to a reduction in checkpoints along Ghana’s transit corridors, particularly on routes serving landlocked Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.
The Authority also successfully hosted the 2026 Annual Borderless Forum with Borderless Alliance, focusing on digital trade facilitation and regional integration.
For 2027, accelerating digital transformation and data-driven trade facilitation is one of five strategic priorities — alongside strengthening regulatory oversight, deepening stakeholder engagement, promoting logistics infrastructure, and strengthening institutional capacity.
